title: Partial Normal Form Semantics

basis.scope: Canonical semantics for partial normal form, reduction outcome classification, and admissible incomplete continuation reduction states after the minimal reduction algorithm is in place.

core_rule.statement: pNF(C) is an admissible, type-correct continuation state whose lawful reductions are incomplete at the current calculus boundary; Outcome(C) classifies REDUCE_025 outputs into NF(C), pNF(C), or classified ⊥C_x; pNF(C) is distinct from NF(C) and from continuation failure; RT_core remains unchanged.

purpose: Formally define the semantics of Partial Normal Form (pNF), distinguish it from complete Normal Form (NF) and continuation failure (⊥C_x), and establish the canonical reduction outcome classification.

canonical_claims.statement: pNF(C) is an admissible but incomplete continuation reduction state.
pNF(C) is distinct from NF(C) and from continuation failure.
Outcome(C) canonically classifies reduction outputs into NF(C), pNF(C), or ⊥C_x.

formal_objects.name: Partial Normal Form
formal_objects.definition: A well-formed, type-correct continuation expression whose lawful reductions are presently incomplete due to the current calculus boundary, while no continuation failure has occurred.

formal_objects.name: Reduction Outcome Classification
formal_objects.definition: The canonical classification of REDUCE_025 outputs into NF(C), pNF(C), or ⊥C_x.

requirements: Additional lawful reductions exist outside the current executable calculus boundary

distinctions.reason: A partial normal form may admit additional lawful reductions in future calculus extensions.
Partial normal form is admissible and well-formed; continuation failure is not.
Normal form is a successful reduction result.

reduction_outcomes.condition: Lawful reductions exist but are outside the current executable calculus boundary

validation_requirements: pNF(C) is distinct from NF(C) and continuation failure.

next_recommended_patch.title: Reduction Trace Semantics
next_recommended_patch.purpose: Define the canonical reduction trace object produced by REDUCE_025, so every reduction outcome records the lawful sequence by which it was reached.
